expectations.text: Notes that External Secrets Operator / Vault keep the secret out of Git entirely, whereas Sealed Secrets and SOPS commit an encrypted form

expectations.text: Mentions that Argo CD needs to be able to decrypt or resolve whichever mechanism is chosen

expectations.evidence: Recommends ESO with reasoning about database-password rotation, and offers Sealed Secrets only 'if you have no vault and do not want to run one'.

expectations.text: Compares the real options rather than asserting one — app-of-apps, ApplicationSet, monorepo, multi-repo, environment-branch — with trade-offs
expectations.evidence: 'Why two repos and not one' discussion, ApplicationSet for the repeating services, app-of-apps for addons ('~10 unique components, not a repeating pattern, so ApplicationSet buys you nothing'), and an explicit environment-branch comparison, plus a Trade-offs section.

expectations.text: Recommends ApplicationSet for the 6 services x 3 envs x 2 clusters fan-out instead of hand-maintained Application manifests, and explains that generators remove the per-combination manifest
expectations.evidence: Matrix generator (clusters × services/*/overlays/*): 'Adding a seventh service is now one directory, not six YAML files. Adding a third cluster is one cluster label.'

expectations.text: Separates platform/cluster addons from application workloads (different ownership, different review path, often a different AppProject)
expectations.evidence: Two repos split by ownership ('Platform addons are low-frequency, high-risk changes reviewed by a different group') with separate `services` and `platform` AppProjects.

expectations.text: Addresses environment promotion explicitly — directory-per-env vs branch-per-env — and notes the trade-off rather than silently picking one
expectations.evidence: 'Explicitly not recommended: environment branches ... branches drift, merge conflicts ... Kustomize overlays make the differences explicit', plus a 'What to do about promotion' section with image-updater and gitops-promoter options.

expectations.text: Warns against targetRevision: HEAD for production regardless of pattern chosen
expectations.evidence: Pins the addons app (`targetRevision: v2025.10.1  # pinned — addons are high-risk`) but never names targetRevision: HEAD as the anti-pattern in this answer; services still track `main`.

expectations.text: Flags at least one anti-pattern relevant to their current layout (e.g. a flat directory of hand-edited Applications does not scale, or mixing platform and tenant resources in one AppProject)
expectations.evidence: 'A flat directory of hand-edited Application manifests has three specific problems at your size' — 36 Applications by hand, no app/addon separation, hand-editing as promotion.
